questions.q: What does sys.dm_exec_query_stats provide that a session ID alone doesn't?
options: Cumulative resource statistics for every cached plan, so you can rank queries by actual cost
The exact login password used by each session
A graphical execution plan directly
A list of every table in the database
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_query_stats gives cumulative, per-plan execution statistics (CPU, reads, execution count) accumulated since the plan was compiled.

questions.q: What does CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(qs.sql_handle) do?
options: Only works on Azure SQL Database, never on-prem SQL Server
Returns the execution plan's XML directly
Calls sys.dm_exec_sql_text once per row, turning that row's sql_handle into readable query text
Deletes the cached plan after reading it
questions.explain: CROSS APPLY invokes the function once per row of sys.dm_exec_query_stats, converting that row's own sql_handle into the actual query text.

questions.q: Which query rises to the top of the resource-cost ranking during the mid-morning window?
options: A backup/restore maintenance query
Billing's invoice lookup query filtering dbo.Invoices by PatientID
A query against dbo.Providers only
A query against dbo.Appointments for Scheduling
questions.explain: The invoice-lookup query against dbo.Invoices, run every time a billing clerk opens a patient record, has high execution_count and high avg_logical_reads.

questions.q: What combination of statistics is the specific signature of a query reading more data than it needs?
options: High execution_count combined with high avg_logical_reads per execution
Zero total_worker_time
Low execution_count combined with low avg_logical_reads
A plan_handle with no sql_handle at all
questions.explain: A query that runs often AND reads far more pages than needed per run is the classic signature of a missing or ineffective index.

questions.q: Why doesn't finding Billing's invoice query explain Scheduling's complaint too?
options: The invoice query never touches dbo.Appointments, suggesting more than one root cause
Scheduling's complaint was already proven false in Lesson 1
Scheduling and Billing use completely separate Azure subscriptions
dbo.Appointments doesn't exist in OverlookClinicalDB
questions.explain: The query found here only touches dbo.Invoices — nothing explains Scheduling's dbo.Appointments complaint yet, hinting at a second real cause.
